They also stated that there will not be an increase in sulphate emissions in MY 1979 for their light duty NPA's (0-6000 GVWR).
Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). EPA questioned the projected increase of 13.7 percent for sulphate emissions. To provide insight into their assessment they referenced their Environmental Impact Statement for the MY 1979 light duty truck emission standard which discusses the issue. This report states, "Current data indicate that there is no substantial difference in the sulfuric acid emission levels of catalyst/non-air pump and non-catalyst vehicles. In contrast, sulfuric acid emissions of catalyst/ air pump vehicles do appear to be at levels generally higher than those for either catalyst/non-air pump or non-catalyst vehicles." However, EPA also noted that they feel the first truck emission standards were set at levels which do not require the application of catalyst technology, and in no case do the standards require the use of catalyst/ air pump technology. They predict in their worst cast situation the annual increase in all catalyst/air pump vehicles would be less than 7 percent.
